title: Named summary drawer
mechanism: For a first-time user, build from the action of completing a reminder: MainPageHeader presents identity and one Resumen disclosure; sections show their own heading and options; TaskCard retains completion, title and Detalles.
visible: Title, selected period, task completion and explicit Resumen/Detalles labels.
disclosed: A summary drawer groups accumulated scope, estimates and diagnostics; task details retain each metadata edit; existing list and section menus stay separately named.
access: Native 44px buttons, labelled dialog, focus return and visible focus.
benefit: Makes the next action obvious without requiring icon literacy.
risk: A drawer may add a step to planning.
verification: Complete a task; open scope and duration breakdown; change a historical period and edit every metadata field at 320px.

title: Context sentence and fact ledger
mechanism: Invert beginner confusion by putting a plain sentence beneath the page title: selected period, own versus included routine scope, and pending count. Section headings use matching sentences; tasks use one due-context sentence.
visible: Identity and concise factual context without separate pills.
disclosed: Ver datos opens a labelled definition list with duration, price, frequency and time-of-day actions, while Opciones retains existing commands.
access: 44px data disclosures and menu controls; definition terms precede values in reading order.
benefit: Explains what the current list contains before the user changes it.
risk: Sentences become long for mixed routines.
verification: Test long Spanish labels at 375px, historical reference dates, own/full counts and the unchanged time-of-day cycling callback.

title: Three disclosure shelves
mechanism: Under narrow-width constraints, arrange independent shelves: page Resumen, section Alcance, task Propiedades. Each opens directly below its own row; never stack glass cards inside glass cards.
visible: Period remains visible; completion and titles remain on plain content surfaces.
disclosed: Page shelf exposes diagnostic and duration routes; section shelf exposes inclusion and breakdown; task shelf contains all metadata actions and links.
access: 44px expanded-state buttons with aria-controls; keyboard focus stays at trigger; reduced-motion shelf expansion.
benefit: Keeps object scope local and makes hidden information predictable.
risk: Expanded shelves can lengthen the virtualized list.
verification: Measure shelf-height integration, 320px wrapping, inclusion toggles and completion without accidental shelf activation.

title: Exception-led metadata with stable details
mechanism: Adversarially test a beginner missing important information: show the selected period and scope at page level, section counts, and a task's due date when it differs from surrounding context; keep a stable labelled details route everywhere.
visible: Completion, title, exceptional dates and active-filter context.
disclosed: All nonexception metadata remains in Detalles; page/section options and summary preserve every statistic and edit action.
access: 44px details buttons; full date accessible name; visible focus; never rely on color to denote an exception.
benefit: Reduces repeated signals while keeping unusual obligations visible.
risk: A mistaken context comparison could suppress a needed date.
verification: Test mixed dates, overdue tasks, inherited frequencies and history; verify details always reveals complete values.

title: Explicit planning mode
mechanism: Invert the experienced planner's fear of losing controls with a page-level Planificar toggle. Default Ejecutar shows clean titles and completion; Planificar reveals header scope, estimates, section configuration and full task metadata simultaneously.
visible: Selected period and Ejecutar/Planificar state; task title and completion.
disclosed: Planning mode exposes existing controls inline with their original callback semantics; list and section options remain reachable in both modes.
access: 44px native toggle, state announcement, stable DOM identifiers and focus retention.
benefit: Offers a coherent intentional switch between doing and arranging routines.
risk: A hidden planning state can confuse a returning user.
verification: Reload each mode, test every menu and metadata edit, and compare 320px execution layout with full desktop planning.

title: Two-column scope ledger
mechanism: For an experienced planner under preservation constraints, use one shared ledger under the page title: Propias and Incluidas rows rather than several badges. Sections follow the ledger rhythm; tasks align name and optional estimate in quiet columns.
visible: Selected period, total pending and explicit scope state.
disclosed: Ledger expansion reveals frequency contributions, completed figures and parallel estimates; task info opens other properties; existing menus remain intact.
access: 44px ledger disclosure, responsive stacked rows, tabular numbers and an opaque fallback to restrained toolbar glass.
benefit: Makes accumulated mathematics auditable at a glance.
risk: Columns can suggest additive elapsed time when some work is parallel.
verification: Verify own/full duration totals, active versus parallel terminology, shopping totals and wrapping at 320px.

title: Scope transaction popover
mechanism: Challenge accidental changes by making routine scope a labelled selector: Alcance: propias or acumuladas. Open a local popover showing both alternatives and their counts before activation. Page and section selectors are distinct; tasks retain direct completion.
visible: Current period, chosen scope and current task titles.
disclosed: Popover contains the existing inclusion callback choices and duration/diagnostic links; Detalles holds all task properties; options remain scoped.
access: 44px trigger and choices, native radio semantics, Escape and focus return; no hover dependency.
benefit: Clarifies the consequence of adding routines before changing scope.
risk: A preview must use existing summaries without inventing totals.
verification: Switch page and section scope independently; compare displayed contributions, history dates and selection after closing.

title: Estimated-work spine
mechanism: Derive hierarchy from a planner's need to judge workload: put the active estimate on a consistent right-hand spine for page, section and task rows; count and period sit beneath headings, not beside every icon.
visible: Titles, completion, reference period and one aligned workload estimate where meaningful.
disclosed: Estimate disclosure retains own/subtask/parallel breakdown; page summary holds scope and status; task details holds other editable properties and links.
access: 44px estimate controls; stack spine below names on mobile; tabular figures and visible focus.
benefit: Makes workload comparable across levels without many competing badges.
risk: A right column can squeeze long titles.
verification: Test long titles at 320px, zero duration, shopping exclusion and inherited/subtask estimates without changing calculation logic.

title: Single task action lane
mechanism: For a distracted user constrained by small targets, reserve the left lane for completion and the right lane for one labelled information button. MainGlassHeader groups navigation and options on one restrained material; section commands occupy their own 44px trailing lane.
visible: Completion, title, due exception, period and separate scope text.
disclosed: Information opens metadata editor routes; page summary opens durations/status; section options retains inclusion and configuration.
access: Nonoverlapping 44px lanes; keyboard order completion then information; reduced-motion scoped feedback.
benefit: Separates completing from inspecting so dense metadata cannot steal a tap.
risk: Information buttons repeat on every task.
verification: Verify rapid adjacent completion taps, nested subtasks, list navigation links and no propagation into row actions.

title: Period watermark heading
mechanism: Adversarially prevent a distracted user acting in the wrong period: give the selected date range a persistent textual heading above all tasks. Page metrics become secondary; sections show only context differing from that heading.
visible: Prominent exact period, list title, scope and completion.
disclosed: A Periodo button reveals the existing navigator; summary retains status/estimates; task details retains all properties and section menus remain visible.
access: 44px period trigger, accessible date range, headings in order and no low-contrast decorative watermark.
benefit: Makes temporal orientation stronger than ornamental badges.
risk: Persistent date text consumes header height.
verification: Navigate to past weeks/months and confirm status, section context and task completion all use the same reference date.

title: Details-on-demand row expansion
mechanism: From first principles, inspecting a reminder should reveal its facts next to its name. TaskCard gains an explicit Detalles expander; page and section summaries use the same inline disclosure grammar without changing task completion.
visible: Completion, title, due date and disclosure chevron with text.
disclosed: Expanded row exposes duration, price, frequency, day-part and links; page/section expansions retain scope, diagnostics, period navigation and options.
access: 44px separate expander, aria-expanded, semantic property buttons and visible focus; no automatic collapse on blur.
benefit: Keeps attention anchored to the selected reminder.
risk: Many expanded rows can create clutter again.
verification: Open two nested task details, edit duration and frequency, collapse safely and verify virtualized heights on mobile.

title: Persistent calm density preference
mechanism: Invert distraction by letting the user choose Compacta or Detallada once through list options. Compacta hides redundant task badges into existing information routes; Detallada restores complete inline metadata with softened spacing.
visible: Title, completion, period and an unobtrusive current density indication.
disclosed: Compacta preserves page/section summary and all task editor actions; special-list facts stay available through labelled details.
access: 44px preference choices; focus remains after rerender; both densities use native accessible controls.
benefit: Gives predictable hierarchy without adaptive rearrangement during work.
risk: A density preference adds configuration and persistence decisions.
verification: Toggle densities with completed, skipped, shopping and life-library tasks; verify no data is lost and 320px fit.

title: Scoped action lists
mechanism: Adversarially assume a screen-reader user cannot infer icon scope: every page, section and task has an Actions button named with its object. Completion remains direct; shared action-list structure reduces visual chrome.
visible: List title, period, task title and direct completion.
disclosed: Action lists retain header controls, section operations and metadata editor shortcuts; inspectable facts appear as labelled values before related commands.
access: 44px named triggers; keyboard-operable lists; Escape and restored focus; no positive tabindex.
benefit: Provides uniform access with explicit object scope in both visual and spoken interfaces.
risk: Menus can mix factual inspection with mutation.
verification: Read actions for two identically named sections/tasks; verify distinct accessible names, duration breakdown and unaltered callbacks.

title: Heading-first spoken outline
mechanism: From first principles, screen-reader navigation should mirror the real hierarchy: page h1 with period description, section h2 with scope description, tasks as labelled list items. Visually replace badges with quiet description lines.
visible: Clear heading outline, completion and one contextual secondary line.
disclosed: Details regions retain metadata edits and links; summary regions retain estimates and diagnostics; all options have explicit scoped labels.
access: 44px controls, aria-labelledby/ describedby relationships and decorative icons hidden; focus visible.
benefit: Makes structural navigation dependable while reducing isolated visual symbols.
risk: Overlong descriptions could become repetitive speech.
verification: Inspect heading order, descriptions for historical periods, completed task state and every property action through keyboard navigation.

title: Definition-sheet information architecture
mechanism: Invert inaccessible compactness by using a single property sheet pattern for each scope. Page, section and task Info opens a definition list; each value has an adjacent explicit Editar action where editing already exists.
visible: Title, period, completion and small but 44px Info controls.
disclosed: Sheets retain scope toggle, totals, diagnostics, dates, frequency, estimates, prices and special metadata without implicit clickable text.
access: Labelled dialog and definition list, focus trap/return, 44px actions and readable text at zoom.
benefit: Turns facts and actions into predictable pairs.
risk: Repeated Editar labels need contextual accessible names.
verification: Read each field/value/action sequence; verify own/subtask/parallel values, related-list navigation and historical status.

title: Semantic one-line status replacement
mechanism: Under screen-reader and glass constraints, replace progress bar plus percent plus headline with one status sentence button in CycleRoutineStatusCard. Page and sections adopt the same count-first sentence; tasks use plain metadata text.
visible: Selected period, count sentence, completion and relevant due text.
disclosed: Status sentence opens existing diagnostic; secondary disclosures retain duration, scope and task editing; options remain separately scoped.
access: 44px status control with complete accessible text, restrained glass only on navigation, polite updates without duplicate announcements.
benefit: Removes redundant progress signals while keeping spoken information complete.
risk: A sentence may wrap differently as counts change.
verification: Test all_done, own-done/accumulated-pending, zero-goal and historical states; confirm diagnostic selectors and duration routes survive.

title: Keyboard command toolbar
mechanism: Derive an action-first keyboard interface with a visible page Comandos button opening a grouped toolbar of existing commands. Sections and tasks keep local action triggers; main content emphasizes completion and headings.
visible: Title, selected period, completion and visible Comandos/Detalles routes.
disclosed: Toolbar groups period, scope, sort and configuration; local panels hold metadata and section operations, with no invented backend actions.
access: 44px triggers, logical Tab order and native controls; optional shortcut always has visible route; Escape returns focus.
benefit: Shortens searching among scattered controls for a keyboard-only user.
risk: A global toolbar can obscure which section a command affects.
verification: Navigate solely with Tab/Enter/Escape; assert explicit page/section names and completion unaffected by toolbar focus.

title: Breadcrumb context rail
mechanism: Invert keyboard disorientation by showing a textual context rail: list, selected period, routine scope. Each segment is a separate labelled control; sections add their local scope underneath and tasks suppress inherited repetition.
visible: Context rail and task completion; section headings remain semantic.
disclosed: Rail disclosures expose existing period navigator, inclusion and summary routes; task details and scoped options retain all actions.
access: 44px nonoverlapping segments that wrap; visible focus; native buttons and descriptive labels.
benefit: Offers a stable path to context changes without cycling through many badges.
risk: Breadcrumb styling can falsely suggest navigation hierarchy.
verification: Check each segment's behavior, selected historical period, section override scope and 320px wrapping.

title: Focusable side inspector
mechanism: Under keyboard constraints, use a persistent inspector on desktop opened by page, section or task Inspeccionar controls; mobile uses the same content in a sheet. Headers become compact and tasks retain completion.
visible: Identity, period, scope summary and completion.
disclosed: Inspector shows all object-specific facts and existing actions, including diagnostic, estimates, section menus and metadata editor shortcuts.
access: 44px inspectors; labelled panel, explicit close, predictable focus return; no focus-triggered automatic opening.
benefit: Avoids shifting the list whenever a keyboard user inspects properties.
risk: Desktop panel reduces available task width.
verification: Test selected object changes, deleted task focus fallback, mobile sheet trapping and every metadata action.

title: Stable focus emphasis
mechanism: Adversarially assume visually quiet controls become undiscoverable to keyboard users: maintain all essential routes in fixed positions, but emphasize the containing page/section/task row on focus-within; never reveal access exclusively on focus.
visible: Stable completion, title, period and low-chrome options/detail triggers.
disclosed: Expanded summaries expose dense facts; focused row gains contrast and descriptive hint while metadata actions remain accessible through details.
access: 44px routes, clear 2px focus outline, no layout shifts, no hover-only commands.
benefit: Helps users locate keyboard position in a restrained visual hierarchy.
risk: Overemphasis could turn every tab stop into visual noise.
verification: Tab through nested tasks and menus; compare unfocused/focused screenshots and ensure controls remain visible on touch.

title: Thumb-reachable context dock
mechanism: Invert unreachable upper controls for one-handed use: add a compact bottom Contexto dock housing period and page summary; top page retains identity; sections keep local options and tasks keep completion/details.
visible: List identity, current period mirrored in dock and task completion.
disclosed: Dock opens period navigator and scope/estimate/status sheet; section and task details retain all remaining operations.
access: 44px dock buttons, safe-area padding, semantic labels and keyboard access; content bottom padding prevents occlusion.
benefit: Moves context inspection into thumb reach without adding task badges.
risk: Dock competes with existing bottom navigation.
verification: Check overlap with app floating bars, keyboard, 320px viewport and last-row completion; ensure one canonical period state.

title: Date-first bottom sheet
mechanism: For one-handed context-first interaction under narrow width, make the displayed date range a 44px button opening a bottom sheet with the existing navigator and current routine scope above estimates. Sections show abbreviated reference context.
visible: Date range, title, count and task completion.
disclosed: Sheet contains inclusion, diagnostics and duration links; task details use a similar bottom sheet while section menus stay local.
access: 44px sheet rows, labelled modal, focus return, safe-area scrolling and opaque fallback to a single glass toolbar.
benefit: Makes temporal context inspectable with broad touch targets.
risk: Combining period and scope in one sheet may be dense.
verification: Switch dates then scope, confirm independent callbacks, test history totals and sheet scrolling at 375px.

title: Touch-safe information gutters
mechanism: Adversarially prevent one-handed accidental completion: move every task metadata edit behind a separate 44px right information gutter; leave left completion isolated. Headers use matching wide summary gutters and explicit section menus.
visible: Completion and title lanes; due exception; selected period and scope line.
disclosed: Information gutter reveals full metadata; summary gutter opens estimates/status; separate section menus preserve inclusion and configuration.
access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, labels and focus rings; no swipe/long-press-only route.
benefit: Keeps dense inline values from intercepting broad thumb taps.
risk: Gutters reduce title width in nested tasks.
verification: Test deep nesting at 320px, touch event propagation, metadata editing and every existing long-press alternative.

title: Sticky active-section context
mechanism: From first principles, a one-handed user needs the current section's context near current tasks. A restrained sticky section header keeps name, summary and options visible; global period remains in the top rail.
visible: Current section heading, small scope/count summary, selected period and completion.
disclosed: Section summary opens estimates/inclusion; page summary and task details retain full data and actions.
access: 44px sticky controls, bounded z-index, semantic headings and scroll margin for focused elements; no decorative blur on content.
benefit: Keeps section operations reachable after scrolling without repeating metadata on tasks.
risk: Stacked nested sticky headings can cover content.
verification: Test nested section depths, focus scrolling, existing drag/drop menus, 320px height and historical context labels.

title: Single-column action stack
mechanism: Constrain large-text layouts to one column: page identity and period occupy separate rows; section heading precedes a labelled summary disclosure; tasks place completion/title above one Details control instead of horizontal badge clusters.
visible: Readable titles, completion, exact period and minimal scoped controls.
disclosed: Disclosure stacks reveal all metrics and metadata as wrapping rows; existing options remain named entries.
access: 44px minimum heights, unrestricted line wrapping, semantic buttons and reduced motion; one shared toolbar glass.
benefit: Protects text size without horizontal overflow or tiny symbols.
risk: Rows become taller and fewer tasks fit on screen.
verification: At 200% text size and 320px, verify every value/action fits, long section names and task completion remain usable.

title: Context paragraphs with labeled edits
mechanism: Adversarially reject large-text truncation: show selected period and accumulated scope as wrapping paragraphs, then section name and pending statement. Task metadata becomes a concise text paragraph with a separate Edit details control.
visible: Complete context text and task titles; completion remains direct.
disclosed: Edit details opens existing property actions, links and breakdowns; page/section options expose remaining commands.
access: 44px edit routes, no fixed-height text containers, full accessible text and visible focus.
benefit: Retains meaningful context without forcing badge-sized typography.
risk: Paragraphs can dominate sparse lists.
verification: Test long localized date ranges, all accumulated states, 200% zoom, shopping cost and related-list links.

title: Native details groups
mechanism: From first principles for large-text users, organize page, section and task secondary content using native details/summary groups with descriptive names. Keep date range and completion outside disclosures.
visible: Titles, selected period, completion and labelled summaries.
disclosed: Opened groups retain scope, duration, diagnostics and metadata editors; menus retain their current objects and callbacks.
access: 44px native summary targets, full keyboard semantics, wrapping labels and no animation required.
benefit: Uses predictable browser disclosure behavior with resilient text reflow.
risk: Virtualized list measurement must account for open details.
verification: Open nested groups at zoom, verify focus and heights, and test section collapse independently of metadata disclosure.

title: Typography-driven contextual scaling
mechanism: Invert large-text crowding by letting typography, rather than pill size, set hierarchy: page title medium, period normal, section headings normal-weight, task title largest within the row; secondary metadata becomes a compact wrapping sentence.
visible: Titles, completion, period and one contextual sentence.
disclosed: Named More information routes reveal all metrics and edits; existing option menus remain 44px even when their visible glyph is small.
access: Em-based spacing, no shrinking fonts, strong focus and minimum targets.
benefit: Creates hierarchy without hiding meaning behind microscopic badges.
risk: Task titles may visually outrank the page identity.
verification: Compare large text on mixed task types, inherited frequency context and every menu at 320px and desktop.

title: High-contrast command bands
mechanism: Adversarially assume low vision makes translucent controls disappear: use opaque command bands for page and section actions, with one high-contrast summary control; task rows use a strong completion outline and labelled details.
visible: Period, headings, completion state and obvious action bands.
disclosed: Summary opens scope/estimates/status; task details retains all editable facts and links; section commands retain existing menus.
access: 44px targets, non-color state text, visible focus and no blur beneath text; contrast tested in both themes.
benefit: Makes interactions identifiable without scattering colored badges.
risk: Bands can visually compete if every section is expanded.
verification: Check contrast, forced colors, all routine status states, mobile wrapping and untouched business calculations.

title: Structured receipt layout
mechanism: From first principles, low-vision context is clearest in a receipt-like structure: page title and date, one horizontal separator, labelled totals; sections repeat a small subtotal; tasks show title plus relevant due line.
visible: Strong labels, tabular pending totals, date range and completion.
disclosed: Receipt Details expands duration, accumulated contributions and status; task information retains frequency, price, time-of-day and links.
access: 44px details buttons, clear label/value relationships, no reliance on striped/color-only MetaSplit parts.
benefit: Makes numbers and scope legible with minimal decoration.
risk: Receipt styling may imply monetary totals in ordinary routines.
verification: Test shopping and nonshopping labels, active/parallel wording, historical dates and low-vision zoom.

title: Magnifiable information panel
mechanism: Invert low-vision overload by opening all secondary facts in a generous information panel with larger text, explicit labels and full-width edit buttons. Page and section rows contain one named inspect route; tasks retain completion/title.
visible: Period and scope, titles, completion and large Inspectar controls.
disclosed: Panel retains all exact counts, estimates, metadata, diagnostic and option links appropriate to the chosen object.
access: 44px actions, scrollable labelled panel, focus management and minimum contrast; no decorative nested glass.
benefit: Makes dense facts readable without increasing every task's visual load.
risk: Inspecting different objects requires additional navigation.
verification: Open panel from task/section/page, test zoom and focus return, then verify all existing property edit callbacks.

title: Shape-and-text hierarchy
mechanism: Under low-vision and material constraints, use one restrained glass navigation surface; plain section/task content uses textual state and shape: checkbox circle, labelled summary chevron, named options button. Remove colored micro-icon emphasis.
visible: Titles, exact period, completion shape/state and scope sentence.
disclosed: Summary and details expose every statistic, property and command with labelled rows; diagnostics remain on the existing route.
access: 44px controls, opaque contrast fallback, text labels for status and no color-only accumulated distinction.
benefit: Reduces optical clutter while preserving distinguishable controls.
risk: Extra text labels can consume narrow width.
verification: Compare light/dark/reduced-transparency screenshots at 320px; exercise accumulated status, estimates and completion.

title: Resume-work compact header
mechanism: From first principles for a busy caregiver, prioritize returning to unfinished work: page shows pending count with exact period and a direct Empezar action; section headings show pending count; tasks show completion and due exceptions.
visible: Empezar, list identity, period and pending tasks.
disclosed: Resumen exposes full scope, diagnostic and estimates; section options and task details retain all properties, links and configuration.
access: 44px Start, summary and detail controls; explicit disabled state when no pending reminders; visible focus.
benefit: Makes resumption immediate without requiring a scan of every metric.
risk: Starting must retain existing eligibility and section scope.
verification: Verify disabled Start, section versus page start, historical periods, mixed routines and metadata editing without changing sequence semantics.

title: Caregiver scope confirmation sentence
mechanism: Invert the risk of misreading accumulated duties: page and each routine section show a concise sentence stating selected period and whether shorter-frequency reminders are included. Task rows show only identity, completion and specific due context.
visible: Exact period, explicit included/not-included wording and task completion.
disclosed: A Cambiar alcance control opens existing scope choices plus counts; Resumen contains estimates/status; Detalles and scoped menus retain all actions.
access: 44px scope controls, full labels, radio state and focus return; tabular summary figures.
benefit: Makes the boundary of today's visible work explicit for interrupted reading.
risk: Repeated scope sentences can still feel dense.
verification: Compare page/section overrides, full versus own totals, historical references and task date/frequency/duration actions at 375px.
